correctness.rationale: The proof constructs the greedy-arch decomposition and a forced absent subsequence, proving that the number of arches is precisely the universality index. Inclusion-exclusion exactly inventories full arches and incomplete suffixes, yielding the coefficientwise rational identity for every fixed q. Algebraic coefficient extraction proves binary maximum-index and first-moment formulas. A permutation-equivariant O_P(sqrt(n)) coupling from iid multinomial words to uniform fixed-composition words, coupled with the iid coupon-collector renewal law and a one-letter Lipschitz bound, proves the normalized limit and expectation convergence for every positive limiting type. The packaged verify.py independently enumerated 48,069 words at q=2,3,4, checking 1,586 coefficients, plus maximal-index and moment identities. Computations do not substitute for proofs of unbounded assertions.

value.rationale: Letter-composition type classes are intrinsic to constrained sequence and fixed-inventory codes, and the universality index is a standard combinatorial feature. The closed rational law determines every joint type-index coefficient for every alphabet, with nontrivial maximal-index counts, finite exact means and a nonuniform coupon-collector limit at prescribed type. This is a natural complete infinite-parametric classification, not a routine single small parameter or a restatement of the unweighted special case.
